SEBI may tighten MTF rules, cap leveraged stock bets to curb volatility: Report

MTF allows investors to purchase shares using funds borrowed from stockbrokers, enabling them to take larger positions than their available capital would otherwise permit.

Curated by: Namit Singh Sengar

Updated Nov 17, 2026 13:16 IST

Photo : ET Now Digital

SEBI is reportedly considering tighter Margin Trading Facility rules to curb leveraged stock bets and market volatility.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 33:14
Instaread
SEBI MTF Rules: The market regulator, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, is considering restrictions on leveraged stock purchases as margin-funded trading reaches record levels, raising concerns about market volatility and potential losses for retail investors.
According to a Reuters report on Tuesday, November 17, citing two people with direct knowledge of the discussions, the regulator is examining proposals to restrict fresh purchases under the Margin Trading Facility (MTF) when leveraged positions in a stock exceed a specified proportion of its free float.
What restrictions is SEBI considering on MTF?
Reuters reported that SEBI is discussing hard limits on the proportion of a company's free-float shares that can be financed through MTF.
Under one proposal, fresh margin-funded purchases could be restricted once MTF holdings reach 5-10% of a company's free float.

However, the proposed thresholds have not been finalised, and discussions are still underway, the report said.
Free float refers to shares available for public trading, excluding holdings generally held by promoters and strategic shareholders.
MTF positions reach Rs 1.53 lakh crore
According to the report, outstanding MTF positions have surged to Rs 1.53 lakh crore, marking a 29% increase from a year earlier and nearly doubling from the levels recorded at the end of 2024.
Nearly two-thirds of these leveraged positions are concentrated in small-cap and mid-cap stocks.

Exchange data cited by the news agency showed that at least 36 stocks have MTF-funded positions exceeding 10% of their free float, while more than 220 stocks have crossed the 5% threshold.
Why is SEBI considering tighter MTF rules?
The proposed restrictions come amid concerns that excessive leverage could amplify market volatility during a sharp correction.
The report added that the regulator is particularly concerned about concentrated leveraged positions and the risk of forced selling when investors face margin calls.
The report also cited lessons from South Korea, where leveraged trading and margin calls have contributed to market volatility.
What is Margin Trading Facility?
MTF allows investors to purchase shares using funds borrowed from stockbrokers, enabling them to take larger positions than their available capital would otherwise permit.
Brokers typically offer leverage of up to four times an investor's capital, charging interest rates ranging from 9% to 18%, brokers said.
While the facility can amplify potential returns, it can also increase losses when share prices decline.
Moneycontrol
Will SEBI ban MTF trading?
SEBI is not considering a blanket ban on MTF trading, it added.
Instead, the regulator is examining targeted restrictions to address concentration risks while avoiding significant disruption to investors and brokers.
The regulator has also paused an earlier plan to expand MTF access as it reassesses risks associated with the rapid growth in leveraged positions.
According to the report, SEBI is expected to release proposals for public consultation before finalising any changes to the regulatory framework.
